identity.industry: Power Transmission & Distribution / Energy Transition Cables

summary.oneLiner: KEI Industries delivered strong Q4FY26 results with 19% revenue growth and margin expansion to 12.2%, driven by robust B2C demand and a 64% surge in EHV cable sales. The core narrative shifts to FY27 where the commissioning of the Sanand plant phases promises 17-18% volume growth, potentially unlocking 25%+ top-line growth if copper prices remain elevated, while the company successfully navigates supply chain disruptions to re-enter the US market.

one-line thesis: KEI Industries delivered strong Q4FY26 results with 19% revenue growth and margin expansion to 12.2%, driven by robust B2C demand and a 64% surge in EHV cable sales. The core narrative shifts to FY27 where the commissioning of the Sanand plant phases promises 17-18% volume growth, potentially unlocking 25%+ top-line growth if copper prices remain elevated, while the company successfully navigates supply chain disruptions to re-enter the US market.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 3,476 cr (+19.3% YoY); EBITDA: INR 424 cr (12.21% margin, +60 bps YoY); PAT: INR 284 cr (+25.5% YoY, 8.18% margin); Order Book: INR 3,585 cr (excl. dealer orders) + INR 233 cr L1; Net Debt: Debt-free with ~INR 1,300 cr cash. One-offs: Q4 exports constrained by INR 50-60 cr due to Middle East shipping disruptions in March; freight costs rising but partially offset by forex gains.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 20%+ CAGR expected (volume 17-18% + price pass-through); Margin: 10.5%-11% (conservative), potential for 50 bps expansion via scale in FY28; Order Inflow: Strong visibility in EHV and Data Centers; Capex: INR 600-700 cr annually for next 2-3 years.
order book & pipeline: Total visible: INR 3,585 cr as of Mar 31, 2026. Breakup: EPC (INR 309 cr), EHV Power Cable (INR 625 cr), Domestic Institutional Cable (INR 2,154 cr), Export Cable (INR 497 cr). Additional L1 pending for EHV: INR 233 cr. Dealer orders (fast-moving) excluded from this figure.
segment / subsidiary detail: B2C (Dealer) sales INR 1,936 cr (+29% YoY, 56% mix); Domestic Institutional Cable INR 804 cr (+6%); EHV Cable INR 188 cr (+64% YoY); Exports INR 443 cr (constrained by logistics); EPC (non-cable) INR 123 cr. Full Year FY26: Net Sales INR 11,746 cr (+20.7%), Wire & Cable value +22.3%.
growth verticals / optionality: Sanand Plant Phase 1 commissioned Dec '25 driving FY27 volume; Phase 2 expected Q4 FY27 driving FY28 volume (another 17-18% growth). US market re-entry targeting 20% export mix. Backward integration into medium voltage compounds (2-year timeline) and galvanized steel wire armor.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded to 12.21% in Q4 despite freight headwinds. Raw material (Copper +16.85%, Aluminum +9.91% avg FY26) fully passed through via tender pricing mechanism. Freight costs to Middle East up significantly in April, but 50% borne by customers; forex gains (INR 90-91/$) offsetting remaining impact.
capex / expansion: Annual run-rate INR 600-700 cr for next 2-3 years. Specific allocation: Sanand Phase 2 completion (Q4 FY27), Bhiwadi land (INR 92 cr) and Baroda land (70 acres) for future expansion/backward integration. Funding entirely through internal accruals.
capital allocation: Debt-free status maintained. Strategy: 60-70% of operating cash flow allocated to capex for 20%+ CAGR growth; 30% retained for incremental working capital. Minimum cash balance of INR 500-600 cr maintained on balance sheet for liquidity buffer.
risks & watch-items: Supply chain volatility (XLPE imports from Middle East disrupted); Shipping logistics constraints impacting export timing; Raw material price volatility (though hedged by pass-through); Execution risk on Sanand Phase 2 timeline; Geopolitical tensions affecting export routes.
management quality / tone: Bullish on domestic infrastructure capex (Power T&D, Railways, Data Centers). Confident in volume guidance despite Q4 logistics noise. Pragmatic on margins (conservative 10.5-11% guide) but highlights operating leverage potential. Transparent about dealer churn (10-12%) and capacity constraints.
non-obvious takeaways: Dealer network depth: Top 5% of dealers contribute 70-80% of B2C sales, while the long tail (2,000+ dealers) serves rural/retail wire demand with high churn. Working capital cycle improving (2.97 months vs 3.39 months) due to channel financing, allowing debt-free growth despite expanding scale. EPC business intentionally capped at 2-3% of revenue to avoid working capital drag.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain disruption for XLPE from Middle East and high freight costs | Polycab India | beneficiary | Med | If KEI faces prolonged logistics issues in Middle East exports, competitors with diversified shipping lines may gain share, though KEI's domestic strength mitigates this. |
| Surge in Data Center and Power T&D capex requiring specialized EHV cables | KEI Industries | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of Sanand capacity coming online just as demand from data centers and grid modernization peaks; EHV order book grew 64% YoY. |
| Volatility in copper prices impacting working capital for smaller players | Unorganized Cable Manufacturers | loser | High | KEI's pass-through mechanism and strong balance sheet allow it to thrive, while smaller unorganized players struggle with cash flow and pricing power. |

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "One of the leading manufacturers of cables and wires with a wide product portfolio spread across EHV, HT and LT Power Cables, House Wire, Stainless Steel Wire", and "Forward integrated into EPC services for Power, Distribution, Transmission and sub-station projects".
- Scale markers on the Overview slide: 9 manufacturing plants across Rajasthan, Gujarat and D&NH; 2,200+ employees (as on 31st March 2026); 2,100+ dealers/distributors (as on June 2026); 2,000+ institutional customers (as on 31st March 2026).
- Healthy order book of INR 42,919 Mn as on July 2026, described as "Healthy Order Book to achieve Turnover and Profitability".
- Low customer concentration: "top 10 customers accounting for 13% of sales in FY26 and 15% in Q1 FY27"; deck states "Diversification helps in de-risking".
- Exports: "Presence in 60+ countries with offices in 4 countries" (UAE, South Africa, Nepal, Gambia); exports also described as a "natural hedge on forex (given we also import raw materials)".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Industry] CRISIL MI&A-sourced view that the India wires & cables market grows at an 11-13% CAGR between FY24-29E, from INR 859 Bn (FY19) to 1,702 Bn (FY24) to ~INR 3,000 Bn (FY29E, midpoint of an INR 2,865-3,135 Bn range); power transmission cables (28-30%) and building wires (21-23%) are ~50% of the market.
- [Industry-Exports] Share of exports in the overall Indian wires & cables market rose from 5% in FY19 to 10% in FY24 and is expected to grow at a 10-11% CAGR over FY24-29E; India aspires to lift its share of the global export pie from ~1% to almost 3% by 2034, with the deck flagging Indian product as "10-20% more expensive vs China now".
- [Brand] IPL sponsorship from FY17 to FY26 plus Pro Kabaddi jersey sponsorships; Super Brand Status for FY 2011-16 and FY 2019-26; Advertisement & Publicity expenses of INR 405 Mn (FY24), 478 Mn (FY25), 539 Mn (FY26).
- [CSR] CSR spend of INR 101 Mn (FY24), 129 Mn (FY25), 158 Mn (FY26), centred on the "Swasthya Utsav" health programme for electricians and their families including free health check-ups and ABHA card creation.
- [Management] Promoter-led board with Mr. Anil Gupta as Chairman-cum-Managing Director, Mr. Akshit Diviaj Gupta as Whole Time Director and Mr. Rajeev Gupta as Executive Director (Finance) & CFO; separate SVP-Operations heads for the Bhiwadi, Silvassa and Sanand plant clusters.
